claim:
Let \(n\ge2\), let \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) be an unknown Hessian, and let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\) be a known gradient. After one exact Hessian-vector observation \(y=Av\) with \(v
e0\), the Newton solve vector \(p=A^{-1}g\) (and hence the conventional Newton step \(-p\)) is uniquely determined over all symmetric positive-definite completions consistent with that observation if and only if \(g\in\operatorname{span}\{y\}\); in that case \(p=lpha v\) for the scalar \(lpha\) satisfying \(g=lpha y\). Consequently, one Hessian-vector observation cannot guarantee exact Newton-direction recovery for every positive-definite quadratic in dimension at least two.
integrity_notes: The general identifiability criterion is proved analytically; a separate standard-library script checks a rational counterexample witness.
The witness is corroborative and is not used as a substitute for the proof.
scientific_limitations: Exact arithmetic only; one Hessian-vector observation and a known gradient at a fixed point.
No quantitative stability bound for noisy products or finite precision.
No lower bound is asserted for multiple adaptive queries or for the full recursive subspace quasi-Newton algorithm.
title: Exact identifiability of the Newton solve vector from one Hessian-vector observation
